chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of al-Hussein ibn Mus'ab, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, God sends down an angel every day and night to announce: 'Stop, stop, O servants of God, from the disobedience of God! Were it not for grazing animals, nursing infants, and bowing elders, He would pour down upon you a severe punishment, and you would be pleased with it with great satisfaction.'
ai.seo_question: What three groups delay God's severe punishment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the concept of *sabr* (divine patience) and the specific intercessors who delay the immediate execution of God's wrath. The 'three groups'—grazing animals, nursing infants, and the elderly in prayer (*ruku'*)—are interpreted by Shia scholars as symbols of natural mercy, innocence, and spiritual humility that collectively sustain the world's reprieve from severe chastisement.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-131 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Mus’ab that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“God sends down an angel every day to announce: O people! Stop disobedience to God! Were it not for pasturing animals, breast-feeding babies and bent back white bearded old men there would have come to you such a hard punishment that would utterly destroy you.”
